question: Is there still an open correctness bug in the shadow (occlusion) traversal, or has it been dealt with? Say what the bug is or was.
answer:
The shadow-traversal bug is closed — it was real, and it was fixed earlier this round.

What it was: in round-2 attempt 1 I added a dedicated any-hit shadow traversal (pt_shadow_hit in shaders/pt_trace.metal) to replace running the full closest-hit intersection for occlusion. My first version returned true as soon as any triangle intersected, without comparing the hit distance against the ray's remaining length (t_limit, i.e. the distance to the light). It only bounded the node test, not the triangle test, so any triangle anywhere along the ray's direction — including geometry beyond the light — counted as an occluder. That over-occluded shadow rays and would have biased the caustic dark, failing the caustic-mean gate.

How it was fixed: pt_shadow_hit's leaf loop now requires `t < t_limit` before returning true (logged as fixed at message #113), and pt_occluded still passes `t_limit - 1e-3f` as a self-intersection epsilon.

How I know it is still correct in the live tree: I read the current shaders/pt_trace.metal in full at #279 while applying a traversal change, and pt_shadow_hit there contains `if (pt_ray_triangle(...) && t < t_limit) { return true; }`. The separate any-hit change I tried later ("test both children, push only hit ones") was bit-identical on the PFM and was reverted purely for performance (478ms vs 64.6ms, #291), so no occlusion semantics changed after the fix.

Note the other open item from that same list, the degenerate binned-SAH partition (7107 nodes for 69451 triangles), is also resolved: it was replaced by the round-1 median-split-on-widest-axis builder (#111-#117), now with kLeafSize 1 and 131071 nodes at depth cap 16 (#316). Both remaining open entries in my working memory are therefore stale.

question: Is there still an open correctness bug in the shadow (occlusion) traversal, or has it been dealt with? Say what the bug is or was.
answer: No — that bug is closed. What it was: in round 2's first rewrite, pt_shadow_hit (the any-hit shadow traversal in shaders/pt_trace.metal) returned true for any triangle that the ray hit without comparing the hit distance against the shadow-ray length, so geometry beyond the light (or beyond the segment to the light) counted as an occluder. That over-occluded next-event estimation and would have biased the floor caustic dark. How it was fixed: I added the `t < t_limit` guard before returning true (writer log entry around message #113, alongside the bvh_stats fix), and the traversal also clamps its slab test to t_max = t_limit (pt_occluded passes t_limit - 1e-3). Evidence it is really gone: the current source I read at message #279 shows `pt_ray_triangle(...) && t < t_limit` inside pt_shadow_hit's leaf loop, and every later run since that fix has produced healthy caustics with bit-identical same-seed PFMs (e.g. #255 DETERMINISTIC, #331 BIT_IDENTICAL) and benchmark timings of 59-66ms at 512x512/64spp. The only shadow-traversal change after that (applying the near-first/push-only-hit-children rule to pt_shadow_hit) was rejected purely for performance — it exploded to 478ms (#291) and was reverted, leaving the correct guard in place.
